verses.en: And inspired it [with discernment of] its wickedness and its righteousness,

tafsir.text: and inspired to discern its vices and piety He pointed out to it the path of good and that of evil the placing of taqwā ‘piety’ second takes into account the rhyme endings of the verses; the response to the oath is the following

verses.ar: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّىٰهَا
verses.en: He has succeeded who purifies it,

tafsir.text: Successful indeed qad the lām of laqad ‘indeed’ has been omitted from it for the sake of brevity will be the one who purifies it purges it of sins

verses.ar: وَقَدْ خَابَ مَن دَسَّىٰهَا
verses.en: And he has failed who instills it [with corruption].

tafsir.text: and he will indeed have failed he who eclipses it he who obscures it with acts of disobedience dassāhā is actually dassasahā but the second sīn has been replaced with an alif for phonetic ease.

verses.ar: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْوَىٰهَآ
verses.en: Thamūd denied [their prophet] by reason of their transgression,

tafsir.text: Thamūd denied their messenger Sālih because of their rebellious nature

verses.ar: إِذِ ٱنۢبَعَثَ أَشْقَىٰهَا
verses.en: When the most wretched of them was sent forth.

tafsir.text: when the most wretched of them whose name was Qudār was dispatched when he hastened in order to hamstring the she-camel with their approval.

verses.ar: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ نَاقَةَ ٱللَّهِ وَسُقْيَـٰهَا
verses.en: And the messenger of Allāh [i.e., Ṣāliḥ] said to them, "[Do not harm] the she-camel of Allāh or [prevent her from] her drink."

tafsir.text: But then the messenger of God Sālih said to them ‘This is the she-camel of God so let her have her drink!’ her drink on her day — one day was hers the next theirs.

verses.ar: فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوهَا فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُم بِذَنۢبِهِمْ فَسَوَّىٰهَا
verses.en: But they denied him and hamstrung her. So their Lord brought down upon them destruction for their sin and made it equal [upon all of them].

tafsir.text: But they denied him with regard to his saying this as being a command from God — which if they contravened would immediately result in chastisement being sent down on them — then hamstrung her they slew it in order to appropriate her share of the drinking water.

verses.ar: وَلَا يَخَافُ عُقْبَـٰهَا
verses.en: And He does not fear the consequence thereof.

tafsir.text: And He does not read wa-lā or fa-lā fear the consequence of it.

verses.ar: وَٱلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ
verses.en: By the night when it covers

tafsir.text: By the night as it enshrouds with its darkness all that is between the heaven and the earth

verses.ar: وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ
verses.en: And [by] the day when it appears

tafsir.text: and by the day as it unveils as it is revealed and becomes manifest idhā ‘as’ in both instances is an absolute adverbial operated by the verbal action of the oath

verses.ar: وَمَا خَلَقَ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰٓ
verses.en: And [by] He who created the male and female,

tafsir.text: and by the One Who mā either functions as man ‘the One Who’ or it is related to a verbal action created the male and the female Adam and Eve or every male and female — the hermaphrodite although problematic for us is in fact either male or female according to God and therefore a person actually commits perjury if he

verses.ar: إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ
verses.en: Indeed, your efforts are diverse.

tafsir.text: Assuredly your efforts your deeds are dissimilar with some working towards Paradise by means of obedience while others in effect are working towards the Fire through acts of disobedience.

verses.ar: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَىٰ وَٱتَّقَىٰ
verses.en: As for he who gives and fears Allāh

tafsir.text: As for him who gives what is due to God and is fearful of God

verses.ar: وَصَدَّقَ بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ
verses.en: And believes in the best [reward],

tafsir.text: and affirms the truth of the best word that is the truth of ‘there is no god but God’ in both places here and below verse 9

verses.ar: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ
verses.en: We will ease him toward ease.

tafsir.text: We shall surely ease his way to the abode of ease to Paradise.

verses.ar: وَأَمَّا مَنۢ بَخِلَ وَٱسْتَغْنَىٰ
verses.en: But as for he who withholds and considers himself free of need

tafsir.text: But as for him who is niggardly with what is due to God and deems himself self-sufficient without need for His reward 929 and denies the best word

verses.ar: وَكَذَّبَ بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ
verses.en: And denies the best [reward],

tafsir.text: and denies the best word

verses.ar: فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ
verses.en: We will ease him toward difficulty.

tafsir.text: We shall surely ease his way We shall pave for him the way to hardship to the Fire;

verses.ar: وَمَا يُغْنِى عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥٓ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰٓ
verses.en: And what will his wealth avail him when he falls?

tafsir.text: And his wealth shall not mā is or negation avail him when he perishes in the Fire.

verses.ar: إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ
verses.en: Indeed, [incumbent] upon Us is guidance.

tafsir.text: Truly with Us lies all guidance the pointing out of the path of guidance from that of error so that Our command may be followed by adhering to the former manner of conduct and that Our prohibition may also be heeded by refraining from falling into the latter manner of conduct.

verses.ar: وَإِنَّ لَنَا لَلْـَٔاخِرَةَ وَٱلْأُولَىٰ
verses.en: And indeed, to us belongs the Hereafter and the first [life].

tafsir.text: And truly to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life that is to say that of this world and so whoever seeks either of the two from anyone other than Us has erred.

verses.ar: فَأَنذَرْتُكُمْ نَارًا تَلَظَّىٰ
verses.en: So I have warned you of a Fire which is blazing.

tafsir.text: So I have warned you of I have threatened you O people of Mecca with a raging fire talazzā ‘raging’ one of the two original tā’ letters of tatalazzā has been omitted; a variant reading retains it tatalazzā that is ‘one that is flaming’

verses.ar: لَا يَصْلَىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلْأَشْقَى
verses.en: None will [enter to] burn therein except the most wretched one

tafsir.text: which none shall enter but the wretched one al-ashqā means al-shaqī

verses.ar: ٱلَّذِى كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
verses.en: Who had denied and turned away.

tafsir.text: he who denies the Prophet and turns away from faith — this delimiting of those who deserve to enter this fire constitutes an interpretation of His saying But He forgives other than that to whomever He will Q. 448 which in turn suggests that what is meant is that entry into the Fire which will be everlasting.

verses.ar: وَسَيُجَنَّبُهَا ٱلْأَتْقَى
verses.en: But the righteous one will avoid it

tafsir.text: The God-fearing one al-atqā means al-taqī shall be spared it he will be removed far away from it

verses.ar: ٱلَّذِى يُؤْتِى مَالَهُۥ يَتَزَكَّىٰ
verses.en: [He] who gives [from] his wealth to purify himself

tafsir.text: he who gives his wealth to purify himself offering it as a means of self purification before God exalted be He by making this payment for the sake of God exalted be He and not for show or the sake of reputation so that he or the offering stands purified in the sight of God.

verses.ar: وَمَا لِأَحَدٍ عِندَهُۥ مِن نِّعْمَةٍ تُجْزَىٰٓ
verses.en: And not [giving] for anyone who has [done him] a favor to be rewarded

tafsir.text: and no one has any favour outstanding with him that must be requited;

verses.ar: إِلَّا ٱبْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ
verses.en: But only seeking the face [i.e., acceptance] of his Lord, Most High.

tafsir.text: but he did this only seeking the pleasure of his Lord the Most High that is to say only seeking to secure God’s reward;

verses.ar: وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَىٰ
verses.en: And he is going to be satisfied.

tafsir.text: and verily soon he shall himself be pleased with the reward he will be given in Paradise. The verse applies equally to anyone who may do as he Abū Bakr did may God be pleased with him and such a person will thereby be removed far from the Fire and rewarded.

verses.ar: وَٱلضُّحَىٰ
verses.en: By the morning brightness

tafsir.text: By the forenoon that is to say the first part of the day or all of it

verses.ar: وَٱلَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَىٰ
verses.en: And [by] the night when it covers with darkness,

tafsir.text: and by the night when it is still — or sajā can mean ‘when it envelops all in its darkness’.

verses.ar: مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَىٰ
verses.en: Your Lord has not taken leave of you, [O Muḥammad], nor has He detested [you].

tafsir.text: Your Lord has neither forsaken you He has not abandoned you O Muhammad (s) nor does He hate you this was revealed when after the revelation had not come to him for fifteen days the disbelievers said ‘His Lord has parted with him and hates him’.

verses.ar: وَلَلْـَٔاخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَّكَ مِنَ ٱلْأُولَىٰ
verses.en: And the Hereafter is better for you than the first [life].

tafsir.text: And verily the Hereafter shall be better for you by virtue of the honours awaiting you thereat than the first life this world.

verses.ar: وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰٓ
verses.en: And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied.

tafsir.text: And verily your Lord shall give you in the Hereafter of good things a bounteous gift and you shall be satisfied with it — and so the Prophet s said ‘In that case I shall not be satisfied if a single person from among my community remains in the Fire’ the response to the oath terminates here with two affirmations and

verses.ar: أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَـَٔاوَىٰ
verses.en: Did He not find you an orphan and give [you] refuge?

tafsir.text: Did He not find you an orphan an interrogative meant as an affirmative in other words He did indeed find you an orphan having lost your father before you were born or shortly thereafter and shelter you? by having your uncle Abū Tālib embrace you as part of his household.

verses.ar: وَوَجَدَكَ ضَآلًّا فَهَدَىٰ
verses.en: And He found you lost and guided [you],

tafsir.text: And did He not find you erring from the revealed Law which you now follow and guided you? that is and then guided you to it.

verses.ar: وَوَجَدَكَ عَآئِلًا فَأَغْنَىٰ
verses.en: And He found you poor and made [you] self-sufficient.

tafsir.text: And did He not find you needy poor and enrich you? and made you content with the spoils and other things which He gave you — in a hadīth it is stated ‘Wealth comes not from the proliferation of transient worldly goods but wealth comes from the contentedness of the soul’.

verses.ar: فَأَمَّا ٱلْيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقْهَرْ
verses.en: So as for the orphan, do not oppress [him].

tafsir.text: So as for the orphan do not oppress him by appropriating his wealth or otherwise

verses.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلسَّآئِلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ
verses.en: And as for the petitioner, do not repel [him].

tafsir.text: and as for the beggar do not drive him away do not repel him on account of his poverty

verses.ar: وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ
verses.en: But as for the favor of your Lord, report [it].

tafsir.text: and as for your Lord’s grace to you by way of prophethood and otherwise proclaim it make it known. The omission in certain instances of the suffixed pronoun referring to the Prophet s from the end of the verbs is intended to sustain the end-rhyme of the verses.

verses.ar: أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ
verses.en: Did We not expand for you, [O Muḥammad], your breast?

tafsir.text: Did We not expand an interrogative meant as an affirmative in other words ‘We did indeed expand’ your breast for you O Muhammad (s) by means of prophethood and otherwise

verses.ar: وَوَضَعْنَا عَنكَ وِزْرَكَ
verses.en: And We removed from you your burden

tafsir.text: and relieve you of your burden

verses.ar: ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ
verses.en: Which had weighed upon your back

tafsir.text: that which weighed down your back? — this is similar to where God says that God may forgive you what is past of your sin Q. 482.

verses.ar: وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ
verses.en: And raised high for you your repute.

tafsir.text: Did We not exalt your mention? For you are mentioned where I God am mentioned in the call announcing the time for prayer adhān in the second call to perform the prayer iqāma in the witnessing ‘there is no god but God Muhammad is His Messenger’ tashahhud in the Friday sermon and in other instances.

verses.ar: فَإِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
verses.en: For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease [i.e., relief].

tafsir.text: For truly with hardship comes ease.

verses.ar: إِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
verses.en: Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.

tafsir.text: Truly with hardship comes ease the Prophet s suffered much hardship at the hands of the disbelievers but then he enjoyed ease when he was assisted to victory by God over them.

verses.ar: فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَٱنصَبْ
verses.en: So when you have finished [your duties], then stand up [for worship].

tafsir.text: So when you are finished from performing prayer toil exert yourself in supplication to God

verses.ar: وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَٱرْغَب
verses.en: And to your Lord direct [your] longing.

tafsir.text: and seek devote yourself humbly to your Lord.

verses.ar: وَٱلتِّينِ وَٱلزَّيْتُونِ
verses.en: By the fig and the olive

tafsir.text: By the fig and the olive that is the two edible foods — or these denote the names of two mountains in Syria on which these two foods grow —

verses.ar: وَطُورِ سِينِينَ
verses.en: And [by] Mount Sinai

tafsir.text: and by the Mount Sinai the mountain on which God exalted be He spoke to Moses sīnīn means ‘the one blessed’ or ‘the fair one with fruitful trees’

verses.ar: وَهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ ٱلْأَمِينِ
verses.en: And [by] this secure city [i.e., Makkah],

tafsir.text: and by this secure land Mecca as people were secure in it in the time of pagandom and are still secure in it in Islam.

verses.ar: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ فِىٓ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ
verses.en: We have certainly created man in the best of stature;

tafsir.text: Verily We created man al-insān the generic in the best of forms in the best proportioning of his shape.

verses.ar: ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَـٰهُ أَسْفَلَ سَـٰفِلِينَ
verses.en: Then We return him to the lowest of the low,

tafsir.text: Then in the case of certain individuals of his species We reduced him to the lowest of the low — a metaphor for old age and weakness at which point a believer’s deeds are fewer than when he was young; but he will still have his reward as God exalted be He says

verses.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ فَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ
verses.en: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for they will have a reward uninterrupted.

tafsir.text: except those who believe and perform righteous deeds for they shall have an unfailing reward one unending — in a hadīth it is stated ‘When a believer reaches that stage of old age which prevents him from performing good deeds then what he used to do is recorded in his favour instead’.

verses.ar: فَمَا يُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ بِٱلدِّينِ
verses.en: So what yet causes you to deny the Recompense?

tafsir.text: So what makes you deny O disbeliever thereafter — after the mention of man being created in the best of forms and his being reduced to the vilest of age all of which indicates the power of God to resurrect — the Judgement? the Requital that will be preceded by the Resurrection and the Reckoning.

verses.ar: أَلَيْسَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَحْكَمِ ٱلْحَـٰكِمِينَ
verses.en: Is not Allāh the most just of judges?

tafsir.text: Is not God the fairest of all judges? the most just of all judges. His passing judgement by means of the process of requital is one such example. In a hadīth it is stated ‘Whoever recites sūrat wa’l-tīni ‘By the fig’ to the end of it let him then say “Yes Indeed! And I am of those who bear witness to this!” ’

verses.ar: ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ
verses.en: Recite in the name of your Lord who created

tafsir.text: Recite bring recitation into existence beginning with In the Name of your Lord Who created all creatures;

verses.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ
verses.en: Created man from a clinging substance.

tafsir.text: created man al-insān the generic from a blood-clot ‘alaq is the plural of ‘alaqa which is a small quantity of congealing blood.

verses.ar: ٱقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ ٱلْأَكْرَمُ
verses.en: Recite, and your Lord is the most Generous -

tafsir.text: Recite reiterating the first one and your Lord is the Most Generous having no counterpart in terms of His generosity wa-rabbuka’l-akram is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the verb iqra’ ‘recite’

verses.ar: ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَ بِٱلْقَلَمِ
verses.en: Who taught by the pen

tafsir.text: Who taught the art of script by the pen — the first to write with it was the prophet Enoch Idrīs peace be upon him —

verses.ar: عَلَّمَ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ
verses.en: Taught man that which he knew not.

tafsir.text: taught man al-insān the generic what he did not know before he was taught in the way of guidance the art of writing crafts and so on.

verses.ar: كَلَّآ إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ لَيَطْغَىٰٓ
verses.en: No! [But] indeed, man transgresses

tafsir.text: Nay but verily man is wont to be rebellious

verses.ar: أَن رَّءَاهُ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰٓ
verses.en: Because he sees himself self-sufficient.

tafsir.text: when he sees it that is to say his own soul to be self-sufficient in terms of wealth — this was revealed regarding Abū Jahl ra’ā ‘sees’ means to see mentally; istaghnā ‘self-sufficient’ is the second direct object; an ra’āhu ‘when he sees it’ is an object denoting reason.

verses.ar: إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰٓ
verses.en: Indeed, to your Lord is the return.

tafsir.text: Surely to your Lord O man is the return — meant as a threat for him — and so He will requite the rebellious one with what he deserves.

verses.ar: أَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى يَنْهَىٰ
verses.en: Have you seen the one who forbids

tafsir.text: Have you seen a-ra’ayta in all three instances here and below is an exclamation of wonder him namely Abū Jahl who forbids

verses.ar: عَبْدًا إِذَا صَلَّىٰٓ
verses.en: A servant when he prays?

tafsir.text: a servant namely Muhammad (s) when he prays?

verses.ar: أَرَءَيْتَ إِن كَانَ عَلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰٓ
verses.en: Have you seen if he is upon guidance

tafsir.text: Have you considered what if he the one forbidden should be upon a path of guidance

verses.ar: أَوْ أَمَرَ بِٱلتَّقْوَىٰٓ
verses.en: Or enjoins righteousness?

tafsir.text: or aw is for division be bidding others to fear of God?

verses.ar: أَرَءَيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰٓ
verses.en: Have you seen if he denies and turns away -

tafsir.text: Have you considered what if he the one forbidding the Prophet should be denying God’s guidance and turning away? from faith.

verses.ar: أَلَمْ يَعْلَم بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ
verses.en: Does he not know that Allāh sees?

tafsir.text: Is he not aware that God sees? what has issued from him that is to say He does indeed know it and will requite him for it. In other words ‘Marvel O you being addressed at the way in which he forbids prayer and at the fact that the one being forbidden is actually the one upon guidance bidding to fear of God while the

verses.ar: كَلَّا لَئِن لَّمْ يَنتَهِ لَنَسْفَعًۢا بِٱلنَّاصِيَةِ
verses.en: No! If he does not desist, We will surely drag him by the forelock

tafsir.text: No indeed! — a repudiation of him — Assuredly if la-in the lām is for oaths he does not desist from the disbelief that he is upon We shall seize him by the forelock We shall drag him to the Fire by his forelock

verses.ar: نَاصِيَةٍ كَـٰذِبَةٍ خَاطِئَةٍ
verses.en: A lying, sinning forelock.

tafsir.text: a lying iniquitous forelock! nāsiyatin an indefinite noun substituting for a definite — the description of this forelock in such terms is meant figuratively and what is actually meant is that individual.

verses.ar: فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُۥ
verses.en: Then let him call his associates;

tafsir.text: Let him then call upon the henchmen of his council the members of his council nādin — a place of assembly where people gather to talk. He Abū Jahl had said to the Prophet s in reproof having forbidden him from prayer ‘You are well aware that there is none in this town who has recourse to as large a council of men as I

verses.ar: سَنَدْعُ ٱلزَّبَانِيَةَ
verses.en: We will call the angels of Hell.

tafsir.text: We shall call the Zabāniya the grim stern angels to destroy him as stated in the hadīth ‘Had he called his council of henchmen together the Zabāniya would have seized him right before his own eyes!’.

verses.ar: كَلَّا لَا تُطِعْهُ وَٱسْجُدْ وَٱقْتَرِب ۩
verses.en: No! Do not obey him. But prostrate and draw near [to Allāh].

tafsir.text: No indeed! — a repudiation of him — Do not obey him O Muhammad (s) and abandon prayer and prostrate yourself perform prayer to God and draw near to Him through obedience to Him.

verses.ar: إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَـٰهُ فِى لَيْلَةِ ٱلْقَدْرِ
verses.en: Indeed, We sent it [i.e., the Qur’ān] down during the Night of Decree.

tafsir.text: Lo! We revealed it that is the Qur’ān in its entirety sending it down from the Preserved Tablet to the heaven of this world on the Night of Ordainment that is the Night of great eminence.

verses.ar: وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ
verses.en: And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree?

tafsir.text: And what will show you what will make known to you O Muhammad (s) what the Night of Ordainment is? — intended to emphasise its great status and to provoke marvel at it.

verses.ar: لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ
verses.en: The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.

tafsir.text: The Night of Ordainment is better than a thousand months in which there is no Night of Ordainment for a righteous deed on that Night is better than one performed for a thousand months without it.

verses.ar: تَنَزَّلُ ٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍ
verses.en: The angels and the Spirit [i.e., Gabriel] descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter.

tafsir.text: The angels and the Spirit namely Gabriel descend tanazzalu one of the two original tā’ letters of tatanazzalu has been omitted in it on that night by the leave of their Lord by His command with every command that God has decreed from that year to the following one min is causative functioning as bi ‘with’.

verses.ar: سَلَـٰمٌ هِىَ حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ
verses.en: Peace it is until the emergence of dawn.

tafsir.text: It is peaceful salāmun hiya a predicate preceding the subject until the rising of the dawn read matla‘ or matli‘ until the time it rises it is peaceful because of the numerous salutations of peace salām spoken in it by the angels who every time they come across a believing man or believing woman bid him peace.

verses.ar: لَمْ يَكُنِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ مُنفَكِّينَ حَتَّىٰ تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَةُ
verses.en: Those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists were not to be parted [from misbelief] until there came to them clear evidence

tafsir.text: The disbelievers from among min explicative the People of the Scripture and the idolaters that is the idol-worshippers wa’l-mushrikīna is a supplement to ahl ‘the People of’ were not going to leave off munfakkīna is the predicate of yakun ‘were’ that is to say they were not going to abandon their ways until the clear

verses.ar: رَسُولٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ يَتْلُوا۟ صُحُفًا مُّطَهَّرَةً
verses.en: A Messenger from Allāh, reciting purified scriptures

tafsir.text: a messenger from God rasūlun mina’Llāhi substitutes for al-bayyinatu ‘the clear proof’ namely the Prophet s reciting pages purified of all falsehood

verses.ar: فِيهَا كُتُبٌ قَيِّمَةٌ
verses.en: Within which are correct writings [i.e., rulings and laws].

tafsir.text: wherein are upright precepts written rulings that are upright that is to say one who recites what contains all that and that is the Qur’ān. Thus some of them believed in it while others disbelieved.

verses.ar: وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَتْهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَةُ
verses.en: Nor did those who were given the Scripture become divided until after there had come to them clear evidence.

tafsir.text: And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided regarding belief in him the Prophet s except after the clear proof had come to them namely the Prophet s — or the Qur’ān which he brought as his miracle. Before his s arrival they had all agreed to believe in him when he would come;

verses.ar: وَمَآ أُمِرُوٓا۟ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ حُنَفَآءَ وَيُقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُؤْتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ ۚ وَذَٰلِكَ دِينُ ٱلْقَيِّمَةِ
verses.en: And they were not commanded except to worship Allāh, [being] sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and to establish prayer and to give zakāh. And that is the correct religion.

tafsir.text: And they were only commanded in their Scripture the Torah and the Gospel to worship God illā li-ya‘budū means illā an ya‘budū an having been omitted and the lām added devoting religion purely to Him free of any idolatry as hanīfs upright in following the religion of Abraham and the religion of Muhammad (s) when he

verses.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ فِى نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ ۚ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمْ شَرُّ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ
verses.en: Indeed, they who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. Those are the worst of creatures.

tafsir.text: Truly the disbelievers from among the People of the Scripture and the idolaters shall be in the fire of Hell to abide therein khālidīna an implied circumstantial qualifier in other words it will be decreed for them by God exalted be He to abide therein — those are the worst of creatures.

verses.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ
verses.en: Indeed, they who have believed and done righteous deeds - those are the best of creatures.

tafsir.text: Truly those who believe and perform righteous deeds — they are the best of creatures al-bariyya means al-khalīqa.

verses.ar: جَزَآؤُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّـٰتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَـٰرُ خَـٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدًا ۖ رَّضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا۟ عَنْهُ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِىَ رَبَّهُۥ
verses.en: Their reward with their Lord will be gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, Allāh being pleased with them and they with Him. That is for whoever has feared his Lord.

tafsir.text: Their reward with their Lord will be Gardens of Eden as a residence underneath which rivers flow wherein they shall abide forever. God is pleased with them because of their obedience of Him and they are pleased with Him because of His reward.

verses.ar: إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا
verses.en: When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake

tafsir.text: When earth is shaken when it is rocked for the rising of the Hour with its final quake with its most violent rocking one that befits its magnitude

verses.ar: وَأَخْرَجَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا
verses.en: And the earth discharges its burdens

tafsir.text: and the earth brings forth its burdens its hidden treasures and its dead casting them onto its surface

verses.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنُ مَا لَهَا
verses.en: And man says, "What is [wrong] with it?" -

tafsir.text: and man the disbeliever in resurrection says ‘What is wrong with it?’ — in denial of that situation.

verses.ar: يَوْمَئِذٍ تُحَدِّثُ أَخْبَارَهَا
verses.en: That Day, it will report its news

tafsir.text: On that day yawma’idhin substitutes for and is the response to idhā ‘when’ it shall relate its chronicles it shall inform of the good and evil deeds committed in it

verses.ar: بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحَىٰ لَهَا
verses.en: Because your Lord has inspired [i.e., commanded] it.

tafsir.text: for its Lord will have inspired it that is He will have commanded her to do this — in a hadīth it is stated ‘It the earth shall testify to every single deed committed by every servant and handmaiden upon its surface’.

verses.ar: يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصْدُرُ ٱلنَّاسُ أَشْتَاتًا لِّيُرَوْا۟ أَعْمَـٰلَهُمْ
verses.en: That Day, the people will depart separated [into categories] to be shown [the result of] their deeds.

tafsir.text: On that day mankind shall issue forth they will depart from the site of the Reckoning in separate groups divided up so that those taking it their book by the right hand will go to Paradise while those taking it by the left hand will go to the Fire to be shown their deeds that is the requital for them in either

verses.ar: فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُۥ
verses.en: So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it,

tafsir.text: So whoever does an atom’s weight of good shall see it he shall see its reward

verses.ar: وَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُۥ
verses.en: And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.

tafsir.text: and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil shall see it he shall see its requital.

verses.ar: وَٱلْعَـٰدِيَـٰتِ ضَبْحًا
verses.en: By the racers, panting,

tafsir.text: By the chargers the steeds that charge in attack and snort with a snorting — this being the name of the sound which they emit from inside them when they charge;

verses.ar: فَٱلْمُورِيَـٰتِ قَدْحًا
verses.en: And the producers of sparks [when] striking

tafsir.text: by the strikers the steeds that strike fire by way of sparks with their hoofs when they gallop across rocky terrain by night;

verses.ar: فَٱلْمُغِيرَٰتِ صُبْحًا
verses.en: And the chargers at dawn,

tafsir.text: by the dawn-raiders the steeds that make raids against the enemy at dawn at the hands of their riders

verses.ar: فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِۦ نَقْعًا
verses.en: Stirring up thereby [clouds of] dust,

tafsir.text: raising stirring up therein in the place of their charge or at that time of dawn a trail of dust by the power of their movement

verses.ar: فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِۦ جَمْعًا
verses.en: Arriving thereby in the center collectively,

tafsir.text: cleaving therewith with the dust a host of the enemy that is to say cutting right into their centre! the verb is supplemented to the noun in the above instances because it serves to explain the verbal action in other words wa’llātī ‘adawna fa-awrayna fa-agharna ‘by those that charge then strike sparks then raid’.

verses.ar: إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ لِرَبِّهِۦ لَكَنُودٌ
verses.en: Indeed mankind, to his Lord, is ungrateful.

tafsir.text: Verily man the disbeliever is ungrateful to his Lord thankless denying the reality of His graces exalted be He

verses.ar: وَإِنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ
verses.en: And indeed, he is to that a witness.

tafsir.text: and verily to that ingratitude of his he is a witness bearing witness against himself to his own actions.

verses.ar: وَإِنَّهُۥ لِحُبِّ ٱلْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ
verses.en: And indeed he is, in love of wealth, intense.

tafsir.text: And verily in the love of wealth he is avid and is therefore niggardly with it.

verses.ar: ۞ أَفَلَا يَعْلَمُ إِذَا بُعْثِرَ مَا فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ
verses.en: But does he not know that when the contents of the graves are scattered

tafsir.text: Does he not know that when that which is in the graves in the way of the dead is strewn when it is turned over and brought out that is to say that when they are raised

verses.ar: وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِى ٱلصُّدُورِ
verses.en: And that within the breasts is obtained,

tafsir.text: and that which is in the breasts the hearts of disbelief or faith is obtained when it is revealed and examined

verses.ar: إِنَّ رَبَّهُم بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَّخَبِيرٌۢ
verses.en: Indeed, their Lord with them, that Day, is [fully] Aware.

tafsir.text: on that day their Lord will indeed be Aware of them Knower of them and will requite them for their disbelief the pronoun reverts to the plural because of the collective import of the term ‘man’;

verses.ar: ٱلْقَارِعَةُ
verses.en: The Striking Calamity -

tafsir.text: The Clattering Blow the Resurrection that will make hearts clatter by its terrors.

verses.ar: مَا ٱلْقَارِعَةُ
verses.en: What is the Striking Calamity?

tafsir.text: What is the Clattering Blow? — intended to emphasise its awesomeness mā’l-qāri‘a both of these elements constitute a subject and a predicate and together the predicate of the first al-qāri‘a.

verses.ar: وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا ٱلْقَارِعَةُ
verses.en: And what can make you know what is the Striking Calamity?

tafsir.text: And what will show you what will make known to you what the Clattering Blow is? — additional emphasis of its awesomeness the first mā is a subject and what follows it is its predicate; the second mā and its predicate also function together as the second direct object of the verb adrā ‘show’.

verses.ar: يَوْمَ يَكُونُ ٱلنَّاسُ كَٱلْفَرَاشِ ٱلْمَبْثُوثِ
verses.en: It is the Day when people will be like moths, dispersed,

tafsir.text: The day yawma that which renders it accusative is the verb indicated by al-qāri‘a in other words by the implied taqra‘u ‘it clatters’ mankind will be like scattered moths like a throng of scattered locusts surging into each other in confusion until they are summoned to the Reckoning

verses.ar: وَتَكُونُ ٱلْجِبَالُ كَٱلْعِهْنِ ٱلْمَنفُوشِ
verses.en: And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up.

tafsir.text: and the mountains will be like tufts of wool like carded wool in terms of the lightness with which it floats in the air until it comes to settle upon the earth.

verses.ar: فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ
verses.en: Then as for one whose scales are heavy [with good deeds],

tafsir.text: Then as for him whose scales weigh heavy in that his good deeds outweigh his misdeeds

verses.ar: فَهُوَ فِى عِيشَةٍ رَّاضِيَةٍ
verses.en: He will be in a pleasant life.

tafsir.text: he will enjoy a pleasant life in Paradise that is to say a pleasing one for he will be pleased with it that is it will be pleasing to him;

verses.ar: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ
verses.en: But as for one whose scales are light,

tafsir.text: but as for him whose scales weigh light in that his evil deeds outweigh his good ones

verses.ar: فَأُمُّهُۥ هَاوِيَةٌ
verses.en: His refuge will be an abyss.

tafsir.text: his home will be the Abyss.

verses.ar: وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا هِيَهْ
verses.en: And what can make you know what that is?

tafsir.text: And what will show you what it is? that is to say what the Abyss is.

verses.ar: نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌۢ
verses.en: It is a Fire, intensely hot.

tafsir.text: It is A scorching fire of extremely hot temperature the hā’ of hiya is for consonantal quiescence and is retained when reciting without a subsequent pause or with; some omit it when reciting without a pause.

verses.ar: أَلْهَىٰكُمُ ٱلتَّكَاثُرُ
verses.en: Competition in [worldly] increase diverts you

tafsir.text: Rivalry in worldly things mutual vainglory about wealth children and men distracts you preoccupies you diverting you from obedience to God

verses.ar: حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ ٱلْمَقَابِرَ
verses.en: Until you visit the graveyards.

tafsir.text: until you visit the graves either in that you have died and then been buried in them or it means to the extent that you actually count the dead as a something to rival one another by.

verses.ar: كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ
verses.en: No! You are going to know.

tafsir.text: No indeed! — a disavowal. You will come to know!

verses.ar: ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ
verses.en: Then, no! You are going to know.

tafsir.text: Again no indeed! You will come to know the evil consequences of your mutual vainglory at the moment of the extraction of the soul then you will come to know in the grave.

verses.ar: كَلَّا لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ ٱلْيَقِينِ
verses.en: No! If you only knew with knowledge of certainty...

tafsir.text: No indeed! — verily — Were you to know with certain knowledge the consequences of your vainglory you would not preoccupy yourselves with it for

verses.ar: لَتَرَوُنَّ ٱلْجَحِيمَ
verses.en: You will surely see the Hellfire.

tafsir.text: you would surely see hell-fire the Fire la-tarawunna’l-jahīma this is the response to an omitted oath; the third consonant of the root of the verb r-’-y together with the second have been omitted and its vowel has been transposed onto the rā’.

verses.ar: ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّهَا عَيْنَ ٱلْيَقِينِ
verses.en: Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.

tafsir.text: Again you will surely see it — repeated for emphasis — with the eye of certainty ‘ayna is a verbal noun as both ra’ā and ‘āyana have the same meaning.

verses.ar: ثُمَّ لَتُسْـَٔلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
verses.en: Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure.

tafsir.text: Then on that day the day you see it you will assuredly be questioned la-tus’alunna the nūn of the indicative has been omitted because of one nūn coming after the other;

verses.ar: وَٱلْعَصْرِ
verses.en: By time,

tafsir.text: By Time! — or it ‘asr can mean the period from the declining of the sun to sunset or it may denote the afternoon prayer.

verses.ar: إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ
verses.en: Indeed, mankind is in loss,

tafsir.text: Verily man al-insān the generic is in a state of loss in all his bargaining

verses.ar: إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّـٰلِحَـٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ
verses.en: Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience.

tafsir.text: except those who believe and perform righteous deeds they are not in a state of loss and enjoin one another to follow the truth faith and enjoin one another to patience in maintaining obedience and in refraining from acts of disobedience.

verses.ar: وَيْلٌ لِّكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُّمَزَةٍ
verses.en: Woe to every scorner and mocker

tafsir.text: Woe waylun an expression implying chastisement to every backbiter who is a slanderer frequently engaging in backbiting and slander that is to say defamation — this was revealed regarding those who slandered the Prophet s and the believers the likes of Umayya b. Khalaf al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra and others —

verses.ar: ٱلَّذِى جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُۥ
verses.en: Who collects wealth and [continuously] counts it.

tafsir.text: who amasses read jama‘a or jamma‘a wealth and counts it over keeping count of it and stores it aside as a provision against the unforeseeable calamities of time.

verses.ar: يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُۥٓ أَخْلَدَهُۥ
verses.en: He thinks that his wealth will make him immortal.

tafsir.text: He thinks in his ignorance that his wealth will make him immortal never to die.

verses.ar: كَلَّا ۖ لَيُنۢبَذَنَّ فِى ٱلْحُطَمَةِ
verses.en: No! He will surely be thrown into the Crusher.

tafsir.text: Nay! — a repudiation — He will surely be flung la-yunbadhanna is the response to an omitted oath that is he will be hurled down into the Crusher that crushes everything that is thrown into it.

verses.ar: وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا ٱلْحُطَمَةُ
verses.en: And what can make you know what is the Crusher?

tafsir.text: And what will show you what will make known to you what the Crusher is?

verses.ar: نَارُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْمُوقَدَةُ
verses.en: It is the fire of Allāh, [eternally] fueled,

tafsir.text: It is the fire of God kindled set ablaze

verses.ar: ٱلَّتِى تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى ٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةِ
verses.en: Which mounts directed at the hearts.

tafsir.text: which peers over the hearts to burn them — the pain of which is much more severe than any other because of the delicate nature of the heart.

verses.ar: إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِم مُّؤْصَدَةٌ
verses.en: Indeed, it [i.e., Hellfire] will be closed down upon them

tafsir.text: Lo! it will be closed in mu’sada or mūsada on them ‘alayhim ‘on them’ the plural pronoun takes into account the plural import of kull ‘every’

verses.ar: فِى عَمَدٍ مُّمَدَّدَةٍۭ
verses.en: In extended columns.

tafsir.text: in outstretched mumaddadatin is an adjective qualifying the preceding noun ‘amadin columns read ‘umudin or ‘amadin and will therefore be inside the columns.

verses.ar: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَـٰبِ ٱلْفِيلِ
verses.en: Have you not considered, [O Muḥammad], how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?

tafsir.text: Have you not considered an interrogative meant to provoke marvel in other words ‘marvel at’ the way in which your Lord dealt with the Men of the Elephant? who was named Mahmūd and the men were Abraha King of Yemen and his troops. He had built a church in San‘ā’ in order to divert pilgrims away from Mecca to it.

verses.ar: أَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ كَيْدَهُمْ فِى تَضْلِيلٍ
verses.en: Did He not make their plan into misguidance?

tafsir.text: Did He not make — that is to say He did indeed make — their stratagem to destroy the Ka‘ba go astray ending up in failure and destruction

verses.ar: وَأَرْسَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَيْرًا أَبَابِيلَ
verses.en: And He sent against them birds in flocks,

tafsir.text: and unleashed upon them swarms of birds birds in droves one following the next it is said there is no singular form for it abābīl like asātīr; but some say that the singular is abūl or ibāl or ibbīl similar in constructed pattern to ‘ajūl miftāh and sikkīn

verses.ar: تَرْمِيهِم بِحِجَارَةٍ مِّن سِجِّيلٍ
verses.en: Striking them with stones of hard clay,

tafsir.text: pelting them with stones of baked clay

verses.ar: فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ مَّأْكُولٍۭ
verses.en: And He made them like eaten straw.

tafsir.text: thus making them like devoured blades? like the leaves of crops which have been consumed trampled and destroyed by animals. God destroyed each one of them with his own stone inscribed with his name larger than a lentil in size but smaller than a chick-pea able to pierce through an egg a man or an elephant and go

verses.ar: لِإِيلَـٰفِ قُرَيْشٍ
verses.en: For the accustomed security of the Quraysh -

tafsir.text: In gratitude for the security of Quraysh

verses.ar: إِۦلَـٰفِهِمْ رِحْلَةَ ٱلشِّتَآءِ وَٱلصَّيْفِ
verses.en: Their accustomed security [in] the caravan of winter and summer -

tafsir.text: their security īlāfihim repeated for emphasis; it is a verbal noun from the verb ālafa for the journey of winter to Yemen and the journey of summer to Syria every year they made use of these two journeys to provide for their trade at the station of Abraham in Mecca in order to attend to the House of God which was

verses.ar: فَلْيَعْبُدُوا۟ رَبَّ هَـٰذَا ٱلْبَيْتِ
verses.en: Let them worship the Lord of this House,

tafsir.text: let them worship fa’l-ya‘budū is semantically connected to li-ilāfi ‘for the security’ the fā’ being extra the Lord of this House

verses.ar: ٱلَّذِىٓ أَطْعَمَهُم مِّن جُوعٍ وَءَامَنَهُم مِّنْ خَوْفٍۭ
verses.en: Who has fed them, [saving them] from hunger and made them safe, [saving them] from fear.

tafsir.text: Who has fed them against that is on account of hunger and made them secure from that is on account of fear they used to suffer hunger in Mecca due to the lack of crops and they feared the army of the Elephant.

verses.ar: أَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى يُكَذِّبُ بِٱلدِّينِ
verses.en: Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense?

tafsir.text: Have you seen him who denies the Judgement? the Requital and the Reckoning that is to say ‘Do you know who he is?’ If you do not know him then

verses.ar: فَذَٰلِكَ ٱلَّذِى يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ
verses.en: For that is the one who drives away the orphan

tafsir.text: That is he read an implied huwa after the fā’ of fa-dhālika who repels the orphan that is to say who violently drives him away from what is his due

verses.ar: وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ
verses.en: And does not encourage the feeding of the poor.

tafsir.text: and does not urge either himself or others to the feeding of the needy this was revealed regarding al-‘Āsī b. Wā’il or al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra.

verses.ar: فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْمُصَلِّينَ
verses.en: So woe to those who pray

tafsir.text: So woe to them who pray

verses.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَن صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ
verses.en: [But] who are heedless of their prayer -

tafsir.text: those who are heedless of their prayers neglectful delaying them from their appointed times

verses.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَآءُونَ
verses.en: Those who make show [of their deeds]

tafsir.text: those who make a pretence with prayers and otherwise

verses.ar: وَيَمْنَعُونَ ٱلْمَاعُونَ
verses.en: And withhold [simple] assistance.

tafsir.text: and deny aid as insignificant as a needle a hatchet a cooking pot or a bowl.

verses.ar: إِنَّآ أَعْطَيْنَـٰكَ ٱلْكَوْثَرَ
verses.en: Indeed, We have granted you, [O Muḥammad], al-Kawthar.

tafsir.text: We have assuredly given you O Muhammad (s) Abundance — the name of a river in Paradise and his the Prophet’s pool around which his community shall gather; al-kawthar also means the abundant good that has been given to the Prophet such as prophethood the Qur’ān intercession and the like.

verses.ar: فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَٱنْحَرْ
verses.en: So pray to your Lord and offer sacrifice [to Him alone].

tafsir.text: So pray to your Lord the prayer of the Festival of Immolation ‘īd al-nahr and sacrifice your offering.

verses.ar: إِنَّ شَانِئَكَ هُوَ ٱلْأَبْتَرُ
verses.en: Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off.

tafsir.text: Indeed it is your antagonist your hater who is the severed one refraining from all acts of good or the one whose line of offspring will be severed by his not having any this was revealed regarding al-‘Āsī b. Wā’il who called the Prophet s al-abtar ‘the severed one’ when his son al-Qāsim died.

verses.ar: قُلْ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْكَـٰفِرُونَ
verses.en: Say, "O disbelievers,

tafsir.text: Say ‘O disbelievers!

verses.ar: لَآ أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ
verses.en: I do not worship what you worship.

tafsir.text: I do not worship at present what you worship of idols

verses.ar: وَلَآ أَنتُمْ عَـٰبِدُونَ مَآ أَعْبُدُ
verses.en: Nor are you worshippers of what I worship.

tafsir.text: and you do not worship at present what I worship and that is God exalted be He alone

verses.ar: وَلَآ أَنَا۠ عَابِدٌ مَّا عَبَدتُّمْ
verses.en: Nor will I be a worshipper of what you worship.

tafsir.text: nor will I worship in the future what you have worshipped

verses.ar: وَلَآ أَنتُمْ عَـٰبِدُونَ مَآ أَعْبُدُ
verses.en: Nor will you be worshippers of what I worship.

tafsir.text: nor will you worship in the future what I worship God knew that they would never become believers the use of the inanimate mā ‘what’ to refer to God is meant to counter the reference to ‘what thing’ they worship.

verses.ar: لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِىَ دِينِ
verses.en: For you is your religion, and for me is my religion."

tafsir.text: You have your religion idolatry and I have a religion’ Islam this was revealed before he was commanded to wage war against the idolaters all seven Qur’ānic readers omit the yā’ of the genitive possessive construction in wa-liya dīni whether with a pause or without; Ya‘qūb however retains it in both cases.

verses.ar: إِذَا جَآءَ نَصْرُ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلْفَتْحُ
verses.en: When the victory of Allāh has come and the conquest,

tafsir.text: When the help of God for His Prophet s against his enemies comes together with victory the victory over Mecca

verses.ar: وَرَأَيْتَ ٱلنَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِى دِينِ ٱللَّهِ أَفْوَاجًا
verses.en: And you see the people entering into the religion of Allāh in multitudes,

tafsir.text: and you see people entering God’s religion that is to say Islam in throngs in large droves after they had been entering one by one — this was after the conquest of Mecca when the Arabs from all corners of the land came to him willingly in obedience to his command —

verses.ar: فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْهُ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ تَوَّابًۢا
verses.en: Then exalt [Him] with praise of your Lord and ask forgiveness of Him. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of Repentance.

tafsir.text: then glorify with praise of your Lord that is continuously praising Him and seek forgiveness from Him; for verily He is ever ready to relent. The Prophet s after this sūra had been revealed would frequently repeat the words subhāna’Llāhi wa bi-hamdihi ‘Glory and praise be to God’ and astaghfiru’Llāha wa-atūbu ilayhi

verses.ar: تَبَّتْ يَدَآ أَبِى لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ
verses.en: May the hands of Abū Lahab be ruined, and ruined is he.

tafsir.text: Perish ruined be the hands of Abū Lahab in other words all of him — the use of ‘hands’ here to denote all of him is figurative and is because most actions are performed by them;

verses.ar: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥ وَمَا كَسَبَ
verses.en: His wealth will not avail him or that which he gained.

tafsir.text: His wealth will not avail him nor what he has earned wa-kasab means wa-kasbihi that is to say his sons; mā aghnā means mā yughnī.

verses.ar: سَيَصْلَىٰ نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ
verses.en: He will [enter to] burn in a Fire of [blazing] flame

tafsir.text: He will soon enter a Fire of flames that is to say a fire that is flaming and ignited this statement is the source of his nickname which was given to him on account of his flaming reddish fair face

verses.ar: وَٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ حَمَّالَةَ ٱلْحَطَبِ
verses.en: And his wife [as well] - the carrier of firewood.

tafsir.text: and his wife wa’mra’atuhu is a supplement to the person of the verb yaslā ‘he will enter’ separated by the clause of the direct object and its qualification — and this was Umm Jamīl — the carrier read hammālatu or hammālata of firewood cactus and thorns which she used to fling into the path of the Prophet s.

verses.ar: فِى جِيدِهَا حَبْلٌ مِّن مَّسَدٍۭ
verses.en: Around her neck is a rope of [twisted] fiber.

tafsir.text: with a rope of palm-fibre around her neck fī jīdihā hablun min masadin is a circumstantial qualifier referring to hammālata’l-hatab which in turn is either a description of imra’atahu ‘his wife’ or the predicate of an implied subject.

verses.ar: قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
verses.en: Say, "He is Allāh, [who is] One,

tafsir.text: Say ‘He is God One Allāhu is the predicate of huwa ‘He is’ and ahadun is its substitution or a second predicate.

verses.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ
verses.en: Allāh, the Eternal Refuge.

tafsir.text: God the Self-Sufficient Besought of all Allāhu’l-samad constitute a subject and a predicate al-samad means the One Who is always sought at times of need

verses.ar: لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ
verses.en: He neither begets nor is born,

tafsir.text: He neither begot for no likeness of Him can exist nor was begotten since createdness is precluded in His case.

verses.ar: وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌۢ
verses.en: Nor is there to Him any equivalent."

tafsir.text: Nor is there anyone equal to Him’ neither match nor comparison lahu ‘to Him’ is semantically connected to kufuwan ‘equal’ but precedes it because it is the object of the intended negation;

verses.ar: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ
verses.en: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak

tafsir.text: Say ‘I seek refuge in the Lord of the Daybreak the morning

verses.ar: مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
verses.en: From the evil of that which He created

tafsir.text: from the evil of what He has created of obligated animate beings and non-obligated ones and from all inanimates such as poison and so on;

verses.ar: وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ
verses.en: And from the evil of darkness when it settles

tafsir.text: and from the evil of darkness when it gathers that is from night when it becomes dark and the moon when it is absent

verses.ar: وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّـٰثَـٰتِ فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ
verses.en: And from the evil of the blowers in knots

tafsir.text: and from the evil of the women-blowers sorceresses who blow on knots which they knot into strings blowing into them certain words but without spittle; however al-Zamakhsharī says ‘with this spittle’ — sorceresses such as the daughters of the said Labīd —

verses.ar: وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ
verses.en: And from the evil of an envier when he envies."

tafsir.text: and from the evil of an envier when he envies’ when he manifests his envy and behaves in accordance with it — such as the mentioned Labīd from among the Jews who were envious of the Prophet s;

verses.ar: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ
verses.en: Say, "I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind,

tafsir.text: Say ‘I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind their Creator and their Possessor they mankind have been singled out for mention here in order to honour them and a preface to seeking refuge from the evil of the one who whispers in their hearts;

verses.ar: مَلِكِ ٱلنَّاسِ
verses.en: The Sovereign of mankind,

tafsir.text: the King of mankind

verses.ar: إِلَـٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ
verses.en: The God of mankind,

tafsir.text: the God of mankind both maliki’l-nās and ilāhi’l-nās are either substitutions or adjectival qualifications or explicative supplements; the repetition of the annexed word al-nās is meant as an additional explication

verses.ar: مِن شَرِّ ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ ٱلْخَنَّاسِ
verses.en: From the evil of the retreating whisperer -

tafsir.text: from the evil of the slinking whisperer Satan — he is referred to by the name of the action waswasa on account of his repeated engaging in it — who slinks away and recoils from the heart whenever God is mentioned

verses.ar: ٱلَّذِى يُوَسْوِسُ فِى صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ
verses.en: Who whispers [evil] into the breasts of mankind -

tafsir.text: who whispers in the breasts of mankind in their hearts — whenever they neglect to remember God

verses.ar: مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ
verses.en: From among the jinn and mankind".

tafsir.text: of the jinn and mankind’ mina’l-jinnati wa’l-nāsi an explication for the whispering Satan being of the jinn and also of the humans similar to God’s saying the devils of humans and jinn Q. 6112;
